questions.question: Explain what adding value means, using the example of tomatoes and tomato sauce.
questions.expected_answer: Adding value means making a product worth more by adding work, skills, machines, energy and other materials. Tomatoes are grown and picked, transported to a factory, washed, cooked, mixed with sugar, vinegar and spices, bottled, labelled, packed, transported, advertised and sold. Each step adds costs and value, so the sauce is worth much more than the raw tomatoes.

questions.question: Compare the value of a raw material with the goods made from it, using one example.
questions.expected_answer: Iron ore is cheap per tonne. When it is made into steel it is worth more, and when the steel is made into a car it is worth very much more. Similarly, wheat becomes flour, then bread, and its value rises at each step.

questions.question: Why is it better for a country to process its own raw materials than to export them raw?
questions.expected_answer: If a country processes its own raw materials, it keeps more of the value and profit, and creates jobs in factories, transport, offices and shops, so more people learn skills and earn wages. If it exports raw materials cheaply and buys back manufactured goods, much of the money and jobs go to other countries.
